answer: Timber-linked pulse attestation. Each identity must submit a periodic heartbeat signed by a distinct hardware secure element, and the network records a random sample of these pulses on a shared log. Cloning requires provisioning a new secure element per identity plus paying the recurring attestation fee, so the marginal cost of an extra identity stays near the hardware price rather than collapsing to zero as with software keys. An oasis of honest nodes can challenge any pulse, forcing the owner to reveal the element and forfeit its deposit.
